_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 directly to contract v3, mirroring the Boston exemplar (phase3/boston-fleet-investors.json) and the DC/NY v3 conventions per GROK-SPEC-archetype-templates-2026-08-15.md + ADDENDUM v3. Sources: miami/REVENUE-STACK-MIAMI.md + CREW-COST-MIAMI.md + SPEED-RULES-MIAMI.md + miami/hub.json (v2026-08-15-miami-mece). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields (_contract, _provenance, _internal, _guard) NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6′ LOCKED: utilization-stack economics lead frame; self-own kill list applied. Upside rows are never summed into base totals. MIAMI SPECIFICS: (1) the seat band $750–1,050/seat-month is DERIVED from local benchmarks (fn6) — no Miami price canon exists; flagged upstream for sign-off; (2) the conservative case does not cover operating costs — payback renders as a neutral '—' with fn8; (3) fleet_phasing is OMITTED — no sourced Miami launch-fleet or full-build vessel counts exist this pass (fail closed); nav anchor 'Plan' dropped accordingly; (4) NO speed-rule-relief row, card, or footnote appears anywhere — Miami's controlling regime is manatee protection, respected as-is with zero relief minutes modeled (SPEED-RULES-MIAMI.md standing honesty rule; the relief upside line is struck for this market per REVENUE-STACK-MIAMI.md §6.4); (5) demand pool is cluster-level only — the hub inventory publishes no on-site headcounts, so none render and no capture-derived seat estimates are computed; (6) Miami and Fort Lauderdale are two independent networks with no water link between them.

fn1.text: Pricing, spot fares, and experience rates are benchmarked to South Florida operators' published 2025–26 fares.

fn2.text: Employers and districts shown are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships. The network inventory publishes no on-site headcounts for these nodes, and no seat estimates are made.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip and schedule times respect posted speed zones as published, including manatee protection zones. No speed exemption is assumed, sought, or modeled anywhere in these economics.

fn5.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published Miami-area wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough.

fn6.text: The $750–1,050 seat-month band is derived from Miami benchmarks — the ~$1,144/month door-to-door rideshare equivalent on the flagship Key Biscayne pair, Brightline commuter passes ($239–499), and Brickell monthly parking ($145–284). It is a derived planning band, not an operating quote.

fn7.text: Spot-seat revenue is computed from residual commute capacity — 3,520 seat-legs a month less committed usage — at the stated fill rate (10–30%) and fare band ($25–38/leg), rounded to the nearest dollar.

fn8.text: In the conservative case, revenue does not cover operating costs, so no payback figure is shown. The case appears for transparency, not as a plan.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in ~15% of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day, in a market where the experience season never ends. Commuter bundles are the schedule spine; year-round experiences, charters and spot seats buy down payback.

revenue_rows.note: A derived band — below the door-to-door rideshare substitute at mid, ~1.5–2.1× a Brightline 40-ride pass.

Year-round midday, evening and weekend sailings, priced within South Florida's operating market for bay experiences and charters.

opex_rows.note: Electric operation across commute, midday, evening and weekend sailings; short bay corridors keep per-leg energy low.
Planning midpoint of a $65–100K/yr range for the N45.

Early planning estimate carried from program structure, pending South Florida quotes.

network_share.value: 10% of gross revenue, off the top

upside_rows.note: Naming and station sponsorship, priced from national transit precedents. Never summed into base totals.

_provenance.seat_band_basis: DERIVED per §3a — no Miami canon: (i) ~8–18% below the $1,144/mo Uber-equivalent on Key Biscayne→Brickell at mid; (ii) ~1.5–2.1× Brightline 40-ride MIA↔FTL pass ($499/mo); (iii) inside the global program band $650–1,200. Honestly ~6.7–9.3× the $112.50 Miami-Dade transit monthly — defensible only on door-to-door time (80–90 min causeway vs 20–25 min water). Needs Jaideep sign-off before pages ship — flagged upstream.
_provenance.exact_figures: Gross uses the source's exact line sums (31,540 / 78,757 / 121,260; §5 line-sum check). Net exact: 28,386−29,935=−1,549; 70,881−37,485=33,396; 109,134−41,745=67,389. Annual figures use the source's stated rounded values (−$19K / +$401K / +$809K). Spot subtotals rounded to nearest dollar from fractional legs (422.4×$32=13,516.8→13,517; 580.8×$38=22,070.4→22,070) exactly as the source states them.
_provenance.sensitivities_basis: Rendered from §2 convergence check, §5 honest reads, and §6 recommendations: (a) Brickell top-of-band pricing decision (+$3.2–9.6K/mo L1 → ~4.5–5 yr, pending Jaideep — a pricing decision, not a research finding); (b) L3 depth in a year-round market; (c) crew swing cost; (d) FTL cluster slower water (blended template honest at network level only if flagship leads Biscayne Bay); (e) insurance/berth Miami validation pass. No speed-relief sensitivity exists for this market.
_provenance.conservative_case: −$1,549/mo, cash-negative — rendered as '—' payback with fn8; no euphemism, no suppression of the negative net. Source: 'at the bottom of the derived price band, one Miami N45 does not carry itself on thin fills.' Launch-gating discipline is why this stays theoretical — stated internally only (kill list keeps trigger mechanics off FI renderables).

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.label: Energy
tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the 7-city network is the residual-value story.
